Jay Mehta’s proposed stake sale in Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) could value the three-time Indian Premier League (IPL) champions at around $1.78 billion (approximately Rs 16,634 crore). According to reports, Mehta is negotiating the sale of 22.5% of his existing 45% shareholding to US-based investment firm Ares Management for nearly $400 million. The deal is expected to be an all-cash transaction and is reportedly nearing completion.

The proposed investment would give Ares Management a significant minority stake in one of the IPL’s most successful franchises. Mehta currently owns 45% of KKR alongside his wife, actor Juhi Chawla, while Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan holds the remaining 55% majority share. If the transaction goes through, the Mehta family’s holding would come down to 22.5%, with Ares acquiring an equal share in the franchise.

KKR Ownership Structure Explained: Shah Rukh Khan, Jay Mehta And Ares Management

Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) are owned through Knight Riders Sports Pvt Ltd, with Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan’s Red Chillies Entertainment holding a 55% majority stake. The remaining 45% is currently held by the Mehta Group, represented by Jay Mehta and his wife, actor Juhi Chawla. However, the ownership structure is set for a potential change, with Jay Mehta reportedly close to selling half of his shareholding to US-based investment firm Ares Management.

Mehta is negotiating an all-cash deal to transfer a 22.5% stake in the IPL franchise to Ares for approximately $400 million (around Rs 3,736 crore). If completed, the transaction would leave the Mehta Group with 22.5%, while Ares Management would enter KKR’s ownership structure with an equal share. Shah Rukh Khan’s 55% majority holding would remain unchanged.

The proposed deal values KKR at approximately $1.78 billion (Rs 16,634 crore) and is subject to formal approval from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), which will conduct due diligence before clearing the transaction. The BCCI is also entitled to 5% of the sale value, estimated at around $20 million (nearly Rs 200 crore). Beyond the IPL, the Knight Riders Group also has franchises in other T20 competitions, including Trinbago Knight Riders, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders and Los Angeles Knight Riders.

Ares Management’s Global Sports Investments: From Chelsea FC to KKR

Ares Management is a US-based investment firm with an expanding presence in the global sporting landscape. Its existing investments include Premier League club Chelsea FC and NFL franchise Miami Dolphins. The reported KKR investment would further strengthen its presence in cricket, although the firm already has an association with the sport through Trent Rockets, a Nottingham-based franchise in The Hundred, which it co-owns with Cain International.

The proposed valuation of KKR is also in line with recent developments in the IPL’s franchise market. Sportico recently valued the Kolkata franchise at approximately $1.738 billion, close to the $1.78 billion figure implied by the reported Ares transaction. Rajasthan Royals were recently sold at a valuation of Rs 15,660 crore (around $1.65 billion), while Royal Challengers Bengaluru attracted a valuation of approximately Rs 16,660 crore ($1.78 billion). These transactions highlight the growing commercial appeal of IPL franchises among international investors.

American investment firms have also become increasingly involved in IPL ownership structures in recent years. Blackstone and Bolt Ventures are among the investors in Royal Challengers Bengaluru, alongside the Aditya Birla Group and Times Group. Meanwhile, CVC Capital, which acquired Gujarat Titans in 2022, subsequently sold the franchise to the Torrent Group while retaining a 33% minority stake. A potential Ares investment in KKR would further underline the growing interest of overseas institutional investors in the IPL.
